subject: Clarify pen-test assertions and evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Sally Reed <sally.reed@atlashealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify pen-test assertions & evidence cadence for order form

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the draft order form — a couple of items on security exhibit and audit rights we need clarified before we can move to legal sign-off. High-level asks from our security team:

- We require a SOC 2 Type II report annually and a written statement that Redwood will share the report within 30 days of customer request.
- We want the ability to request a penetration test (either Atlas-led or third-party) with a 30-day notice. We need clarity on scope (IP ranges, production vs. staging), whether Redwood will permit active testing against production routes, and what controls are available to limit blast radius.
- Evidence cadence: be explicit about what artifacts are available on request (audit logs, access logs, config snapshots, redacted vulnerability reports) and typical delivery timelines.
- We are also concerned about overly broad audit rights in the MSA: our GC flagged language that allows "on-site inspection" and unlimited access; that will need to be narrowed.

Attached is our security questionnaire (Atlas_Security_Questions.xlsx) with the items that prompted these asks. Can you confirm Redwood's position on: SOC2 availability, pen-test windows, production testing policy, and a proposed evidence delivery SLA (e.g., 10 business days for SOC2, 5 business days for log extracts)?

Appreciate a concrete proposal so we can run internally.

Thanks — Sally

Sally Reed
Sr. Security Program Manager | AtlasHealth
Sally.Reed@atlashealth.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sally Reed <sally.reed@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@atlashealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pen-test assertions & evidence cadence for order form

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. I pulled the security team and legal in so we can propose a single consolidated path forward. Summary of Redwood's position and our proposed compromise below; attaching two docs: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_draft_v3.pdf and PenTest_Scope_Proposal.xlsx.

Proposed compromises (high level):
- SOC 2: Redwood will provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report upon execution of the order form / NDA and again annually. We can commit to making the report available within 10 business days of a formal request (sensitive customer data redacted as needed).
- Pen test: We agree to a pen-test but require it be scoped and scheduled with Redwood security and operational leads. We can accept customer-requested tests no more than once per 12-month period. Notice: 30 days preferred but we will allow a shorter operational scheduling window if mutually agreed (we propose a 30-day baseline). Active testing against production is allowed only if: (a) the test plan is pre-approved, (b) testing is non-destructive, and (c) Redwoods retains final veto on tests that materially risk service availability.
- Audit rights: We will narrow MSA language to timeboxed, scope-limited audit rights: access via secure evidence delivery, no unfettered on-site inspections for hosted customers, and any access to systems requires a signed NDA and SOW for on-prem customers.
- Evidence cadence: Proposed timelines: SOC2 report (10 business days), redacted vulnerability summary (5 business days), access/log extracts (7 business days), pen-test final report (10 business days after vendor delivery).

Would you review the attached exhibit and scope sheet and let me know which parts are blockers for Atlas? If OK, legal (cc'd karthik) will provide line-level language for the MSA/order form to reflect these commitments.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_draft_v3.pdf (pdf); PenTest_Scope_Proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify pen-test assertions & evidence cadence for order form (internal redlines)

Naomi / team — thanks for pulling this together. Below are the legal redlines and talking points I recommend we present to Atlas. I pasted a candidate clause they can accept instead of the broad language currently in the MSA. Use this when we reply.

Candidate MSA clause (proposed):
"Audit and Assurance: Customer may request Redwood's most recent SOC 2 Type II report and Redwood will deliver such report (redacted for third-party vendor and customer-identifiable data) within ten (10) business days of a written request. Customer may request a penetration test no more than once in any rolling twelve (12) month period. Any such test shall be: (a) limited to pre-agreed IP addresses and endpoints listed in an approved scope; (b) non-destructive in nature; (c) scheduled with at least thirty (30) days' advance notice; and (d) coordinated through Redwood's security point of contact. Testing of production systems is permitted only where expressly agreed in writing and subject to Redwood's operational constraints. On-site inspections of Redwood-hosted facilities are not permitted; for customers with on-prem or dedicated-hosted deployments, limited on-site inspections may be permitted under a separate SOW and NDA. Delivery of evidence will be via secure link or encrypted transmission and Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to deliver requested artifacts within the timelines set forth in the security exhibit."

Negotiation talking points:
- Push for timeboxed, one-request-per-12-month limit on pen tests.
- Insist on pre-approved test plans and vendor accreditation (no random, unsupervised testing).
- Refuse unlimited on-site access for hosted customers; offer audit reports and remote evidence instead.
- Agree to defined evidence categories with delivery SLAs rather than ad hoc "any evidence" requests.

If you want I can produce a redlined MSA snippet (tracked changes) and a clean exhibit to share.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sally Reed <sally.reed@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@atlashealth.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed final language and scheduling for SOC2 / pen-test (redlines attached)

Sally — following legal review I wanted to share the consolidated language and operational plan for Atlas to review. Key points (short):

- SOC2: Redwood will deliver the latest SOC 2 Type II report within 10 business days of a written request. We will redact third-party vendor specifics and customer-identifiable data.
- Pen Test: Limited to once per 12 months (customer may request, Redwood must approve scope). Baseline notice = 30 days and the test is non-destructive. Production testing allowed only if expressly agreed in writing and with a jointly-approved plan.
- Evidence delivery: timelines we can commit to — redacted vulnerability summary (5 business days), access/log extracts (7 business days), pen-test final report (10 business days after vendor sign-off). Evidence will be delivered via a secure link or SFTP.

Snippets attached: 1) clean security exhibit you can include with the order form, 2) tracked redlines for the MSA. If Atlas agrees to the above, we can include the exhibit and proceed to order signature. If you need a slightly tighter pen-test cadence, tell us the business reason and we'll see if we can narrow the 12-month limit for strategic customers.

Next steps:
- Please confirm acceptance of the language above or indicate specific lines you cannot accept.
- If accepted, we will update the order form and push for signature.

Link to proposed exhibit: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/s/Redwood_Security_Exhibit_draft_v3
DocuSign (for order form) will be sent once we have mutual language.

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_draft_v3.pdf (pdf); PenTest_Scope_Proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sally Reed <sally.reed@atlashealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed final language and scheduling for SOC2 / pen-test (redlines attached)

Naomi — thanks and appreciated the level of detail. Atlas accepts the proposed language with one minor ask: please add a line that Redwood will provide a 7 business-day notification of any planned maintenance or scheduled tests that might affect availability so we can coordinate on any high-impact windows. Otherwise we are comfortable moving forward; PO attached.

Sally
Sally Reed
Sr. Security Program Manager | AtlasHealth
Attachments: PO_Atlas_5791.pdf (pdf)
